reference.title: Haystack smart tag dictionary
reference.shortdesc: This module provides the Haystack smart tag dictionary.

section.p: The Haystack dictionary is indicated by the hs or h4 namespace followed by a colon character (:). The haystack module contains the types of components typically present in any smart tag dictionary (tag definitions, tag group definitions, relation definitions, and tag rules). ProjectHaystack.org created and maintains the Haystack tags and equipment point tag groups. As part of that, the organization frequently adds and removes tag definitions. Periodically, a new or updated Niagara release provides the updated haystack module. However, an alternative is available for customers who do not want the updated module or who cannot upgrade software for their whole station.
section.note: In , when a Haystack tag dictionary is already installed in a station it is no longer imported automatically when the station starts after upgrading the haystack module. This change prevents any new implied equipRef and siteRef relations from appearing in the station and affecting hierarchies and NEQL results. The latest tag, tag group, and relation definitions can be imported by invoking the Import Dictionary action on the HsTagDictionary component.

fig.title: Haystack palette contains 2 versions of the dictionary

section.p: In , the haystack palette provides two versions of the dictionary: one containing only standard items and another containing the implied equipRef and siteRef smart relations. When adding a new Haystack tag dictionary to a station, the version that includes smart relations is recommended to take advantage of Haystack's automated semantic relationships. Both dictionary variants are maintained and imported using JSON files only. The smart‑relations version references a JSON-based import file packaged with the haystack module.

In earlier versions, Haystack tag definitions could be modified using external CSV files and the haystack‑rt patch jar. In the current version, all tag dictionary import, export, and modification operations use JSON exclusively. CSV-based workflows are no longer supported.To modify the Haystack dictionary:
Export the dictionary as a JSON file.
Edit the JSON file using a JSON‑aware editor.
Reimport the modified JSON using the Import Dictionary action.The installed Haystack dictionary version number is visible in the property sheet. If a modified dictionary is imported using the same version number, appends (import) to indicate that locally modified content has been applied.
